title: Do 3D Large Language Models Really Understand 3D Spatial Relationships?
claim: Existing models answer correctly even without 3D input, hiding real failures; a stricter benchmark exposes this and our training method fixes it.
layout: 3 zones: scene and questions, answer grid by model, right-side bar chart
description: The left side shows a top-down 3D room scene above four columns of situation statements and questions in lavender boxes. Below them is a grid of answer boxes for three rows of models: 3D-LLM with 3D input (pink label), Blind LLM with no 3D input (cream label), and Ours, the 3D-aware model (green label). Each row has a small robot icon. Correct answers have green frames and wrong answers have red frames. The first column is correct for all three models, which illustrates a 3D-independent question. On the right, under the heading 'Real-3DQA Benchmark & Solution', three green checkmarks list the contributions. Below them is a horizontal bar chart comparing SQA3D (light purple) with Real-3DQA (dark purple) performance. The Real-3DQA bars are much shorter for the baselines and recover for the proposed model.
caption: Our Real-3DQA Benchmark and Solution. We demonstrate the answer differences between 3D-LLM (LEO) and its blind-finetuned version on various questions, with correct answers highlighted in green frames and incorrect ones in red frames. We discover that some questions can be answered correctly regardless of whether 3D information is used, which we consider to be 3D-independent questions. By filtering out these 3D-independent questions and introducing a new viewpoint rotation score, the original models' performance drops significantly on Real-3DQA. Finally, using our proposed 3D-aware Reweighted Finetuning strategy, performance improves again.
abstract: Recent 3D Large-Language Models (3D-LLMs) claim to understand 3D worlds, especially spatial relationships among objects. Yet, we find that simply fine-tuning a language model on text-only question-answer pairs can perform comparably or even surpass these methods on the SQA3D benchmark without using any 3D input. This indicates that the SQA3D benchmark may not be able to detect if the model exploits textual shortcuts rather than engages in 3D-aware reasoning. To address this issue, we introduce Real-3DQA, a more rigorous evaluation benchmark that filters out easy-to-guess questions and introduces a structured taxonomy to assess various aspects of 3D reasoning. Experiments on Real-3DQA confirm that existing 3D-LLMs struggle with spatial relationships once simple cues are removed. We further propose a 3D-reweighted training objective that guides model to rely more on 3D visual clues, substantially enhancing 3D-LLMs performance in spatial reasoning tasks. Our findings underscore the need for robust benchmarks and tailored training strategies to advance genuine 3D vision-language understanding. Project page: https://real-3dqa.github.io/.
